scope: Placed-memory capability presence on the Android Vulkan loader path used by this repo's emulator runs. A standalone offscreen fixture loads /system/lib64/libvulkan.so through vkGetInstanceProcAddr, creates an instance and a minimal device, enumerates instance/device extensions and queries VkPhysicalDeviceFeatures2 with VkPhysicalDeviceMapMemoryPlacedFeaturesEXT chained. It records whether VK_EXT_map_memory_placed is advertised and whether memoryMapPlaced/memoryMapRangePlaced are true, so the capability-SKIP branch of the loader-path qualification lane is data-backed instead of assumed. No game, app, window, mapping or GPU workload is involved.

fixture.kind: standalone C fixture, VK_NO_PROTOTYPES + dlopen + vkGetInstanceProcAddr, no build-system dependency
behaviour: dlopen(LIBRARY) and resolve vkGetInstanceProcAddr; if only vk_icdGetInstanceProcAddr exists it is used and printed as LOADER_ENTRY so a direct-ICD load is never mistaken for the loader path.
vkEnumerateInstanceVersion, then a 1.1+ instance (clamped to 1.3) with a retry ladder 1.2/1.1/1.0; VK_KHR_get_physical_device_properties2 is enabled only for a 1.0 instance when available.
Enumerates instance extensions, physical devices, device extensions, and prints all names with --print-all.
vkGetPhysicalDeviceProperties2 with VkPhysicalDeviceDriverProperties (API 1.2+) for driver name/info.
vkGetPhysicalDeviceFeatures2 chained with VkPhysicalDeviceMapMemoryPlacedFeaturesEXT: query only, the feature is never enabled.
Prints three base-feature positive controls (robustBufferAccess, samplerAnisotropy, textureCompressionBC) so all-zero placed bits cannot be confused with a silently empty query response.
Creates a minimal feature-less device with one queue, then destroys device, instance and library.

Exit 0 when the queries complete; exit 1 with FAIL lines only for a real loader/instance/device failure. Prints RESULT=SUPPORTED when the extension is advertised and memoryMapPlaced is true, otherwise RESULT=SKIP with a REASON.

fixture_binary.toolchain: Android NDK r27d 27.3.13750724, aarch64-linux-android34-clang, 16 KB max/common page-size link flags
fixture_binary.vulkan_headers: <workspace>/Documents/Codex/2026-10-13/82379689/work/turnip-refactor-qualification/wrapper-build/source/include (Vulkan-Headers header version 289, which defines VK_EXT_map_memory_placed; the NDK r27d sysroot header version 275 predates the extension)
fixture_binary.deterministic: A second identical build from the same source path produced the identical sha256.
fixture_binary.api_genericity: The same binary was executed unchanged on API 36 (loader API 1.4.0, device API 1.3.0) and API 37; the instance-API retry ladder and core/KHR features2 fallback make it work on 1.0/1.1+ loaders.

build_command_source_note: The 4 KB native receipt docs/evidence/2026-10-21-vulkan-wrapper-native-4k.json records the probe source and binary hashes but does not embed an ndk/clang command line. The identical r27d recipe recorded in docs/evidence/2026-10-21-vulkan-wrapper-native-16k.json (same compiler, flags, header include dir and 16 KB link flags) was used verbatim for this fixture.

per_avd.Vapor_UI_API36 (4 KB, Android 16/API 36): VK_EXT_map_memory_placed absent from a 49-entry device extension list; features2 chained query completed with memoryMapPlaced=0, memoryMapRangePlaced=0; CAPABILITY=absent, RESULT=SKIP.
per_avd.Vapor_API_37_16KB (16 KB, Android 17/API: VK_EXT_map_memory_placed absent from a 101-entry device extension list; features2 chained query completed with memoryMapPlaced=0, memoryMapRangePlaced=0; CAPABILITY=absent, RESULT=SKIP.

conclusion.skip_semantics: Absent capability means the loader-path qualification lane must report SKIP (not FAIL and not a placed-memory pass) on these Android emulator paths. The fixture printed RESULT=SKIP with REASON=extension-not-advertised on both AVDs, matching the harness gate contract. The base-feature positive controls returned true, so the zeroed placed bits reflect driver capability, not an empty/failed query.
conclusion.why_honest: The Android emulator GPUs are software paths (llvmpipe on the 4 KB AVD; gfxstream forwarding to host llvmpipe on the 16 KB AVD). Neither implements placed memory, so treating placed-memory coverage as 'skipped' on this platform is accurate. Real placed-memory semantics still require a RADV/ANV/NVK/Turnip-class driver and physical hardware; this receipt records absence only and claims no placed-memory validation.
conclusion.not_a_regression: VK_EXT_map_memory_placed is a device extension provided by the ICD, not the loader: the loader path is proven by LOADER_ENTRY=vkGetInstanceProcAddr and LOADER_API=1.4.0 on both AVDs, while the underlying drivers (Mesa llvmpipe 26.0.0-devel / gfxstream Mesa 26.2.0-devel) do not advertise it.

related_evidence: docs/evidence/2026-10-21-vulkan-wrapper-staging.json (open item O1: the placed-memory staging double-free class is only reachable when memoryMapPlaced is enabled; these AVDs cannot exercise it, so that open item stays untested here)
docs/evidence/2026-10-21-wrapper-staging-reclaim.json (staging reclaim patch; its placed-memory path was not runtime-validated)

docs/evidence/2026-10-21-vulkan-wrapper-native-4k.json and docs/evidence/2026-10-21-vulkan-wrapper-native-16k.json (the same two AVDs and staging/launch pattern used by the earlier native wrapper probes)
Loader-path harness lane (no-GPU CI lane): its capability gate must SKIP when this fixture reports RESULT=SKIP.
limitations: Emulator software Vulkan only: llvmpipe (4 KB AVD) and gfxstream forwarding to host llvmpipe (16 KB AVD); no RADV/ANV/NVK/Turnip and no physical GPU or phone.
The fixture queries capability only; it never enables VK_EXT_map_memory_placed, never calls vkMapMemory2/vkMemoryMapPlacedInfoEXT and never performs a placed mapping.
Absence here does not predict absence on a physical Adreno/Mali/Turnip path; the same binary can be run with a different library path to check those drivers, but that was not done.
Only the normal Android loader path was exercised (dlopen of /system/lib64/libvulkan.so). The result is therefore about that path, not about a host loader or an explicit VK_ICD_FILENAMES selection.
Two runs per AVD (summary and --print-all) in one boot window each; this is a capability observation, not a stability or concurrency test.
The API 36 AVD runs a 4 KB system image; the API 37 AVD runs a 16 KB image. Page size is not isolated from Android API level in this comparison (both results are identical SKIPs).
No performance, game, app or rendering claim is made; no Vapor app, asset, APK or release output was changed.
